title: DDCA Calls DPL Corruption Claims Unverified, Refers Matter to Authorities
excerpt: The association says Tehelka's match-fixing allegations are unsubstantiated and has asked the authorities to examine the matter through due process.
body:
• The Delhi and District Cricket Association said on September 22 that reports of corruption in the Delhi Premier League are "unverified and unsubstantiated."
  • The DDCA said it has written to the relevant authorities, asking that the matter be examined through established processes.
  • The claims stem from a Tehelka sting in which former Ranji player Rachit Bhatia allegedly boasted of spot-fixing access in the DPL.
  • Former Chennai Super Kings player Vansh Bedi told the anti-corruption unit he was approached to leak team information during DPL 2026.

What the sting alleged

The controversy began with an investigative report by Tehelka, which quoted former Ranji Trophy cricketer Rachit Bhatia claiming he had inside access to team information and the ability to facilitate spot-fixing in the Delhi Premier League. According to reports on the sting, Bhatia, unaware he was being filmed, said he could supply playing XIs before the toss and claimed to have previously shared sensitive information with bookies during the 2025 IPL season, as well as engaging in fixing during the Syed Mushtaq Ali Tournament. One report put his alleged price at Rs 40 lakh per instance of information.

The match under the spotlight was Game 7 of the tournament's third edition, played between Central Delhi Kings and North Delhi Strikers at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, according to IANS. The recently concluded DPL 2026 season ended with South Delhi Superstarz beating Central Delhi Kings by seven wickets in the final on August 30.

DDCA's response: unverified, refer to authorities

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the DDCA said it had taken note of reports concerning alleged irregularities involving certain players and a franchise, without naming any individual or team. The association's position was unambiguous:

"The Association believes it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions about any individual, player or franchise based solely on such allegations."

— DDCA statement, September 22

The statement stressed that the allegations have not been established by any competent authority, and said the DDCA has shared what it knows with the relevant authorities, requesting examination "through the appropriate established processes." It added that the association maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward anything compromising cricket's integrity and will cooperate fully with any inquiry, with action to follow strictly on the findings of the competent authorities.

The Bedi disclosure to the anti-corruption unit

Separately, SportsTak reported that Vansh Bedi, a Central Delhi Kings player, informed the BCCI's anti-corruption unit that he had been approached by Bhatia to leak inside information about the team during DPL 2026. Bedi was part of the Chennai Super Kings squad in IPL 2025 after being picked for Rs 55 lakh in the mega auction, though an injury ruled him out of the season, and he went unsold this year. His disclosure, made through official channels, gives investigators a first-hand account to work with beyond the sting footage.

What happens next

Cricinfo reported that it has sought comment from BCCI anti-corruption head Sharad Kumar. The DDCA, for its part, has drawn a firm line between allegation and established fact and says it will let due process take its course. Until the authorities the DDCA has written to complete their examination, the claims remain exactly what the association calls them: unverified. For a league trying to establish itself as a credible rung below the IPL, how this inquiry is handled will matter as much as its outcome.
nri_angle: Domestic T20 league integrity feeds directly into the IPL pipeline that diaspora fans follow closely; how the DDCA handles this inquiry will shape trust in the system.
author: Diaspora Desk
